question: A nurse carefully documents every single dressing change and item used on a patient's chart. How does this affect hospital financing?

options.A: It automatically increases the national tax rate for citizens
options.B: It forces the government to stop using donor funds
options.C: It guarantees the patient will be discharged the same day
options.D: It ensures accurate billing and prevents loss of facility revenue

explanation: Good documentation means the hospital accurately accounts for every service given, ensuring proper insurance reimbursement and keeping the clinic funded to help the next patient. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h7)

question: Which of these is a leading direct cause of maternal death worldwide?

options.A: Mild joint stiffness
options.B: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Benign skin rashes
options.D: Common seasonal influenza

explanation: Heavy bleeding after delivery (postpartum hemorrhage) is one of the top dangers new mothers face globally. Knowing how to manage it is key for every nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h5)

question: As a nurse, what common myth about weakness in cancer patients should you avoid?

options.A: Thinking it has no relationship to chemotherapy
options.B: Assuming it is simply due to aging or lack of effort
options.C: Believing it can only be cured by heavy weightlifting
options.D: Stating that it always resolves immediately after surgery

explanation: Never assume a weak patient is just being lazy or getting old! Cancer weakness comes from the disease, poor nutrition, and heavy treatments. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h4)

question: What is a major, non-negotiable requirement for a patient who has received a successful kidney transplant?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of physical activity to protect the new incision site
options.B: Undergoing hemodialysis twice a week to clean the transplanted organ
options.C: Following a strict low-protein diet for the rest of their natural life
options.D: Taking lifelong immunosuppressive medications to prevent organ rejection

explanation: The body's immune system naturally views a new organ as a stranger and tries to fight it. Transplant patients must take anti-rejection drugs every single day to protect their new kidney. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h6)

question: A patient recovering from a bacterial gut infection comes back weeks later with painful, swollen joints. What is this likely called?

options.A: Septic joint infection
options.B: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.C: Reactive arthritis
options.D: Osteoarthritis

explanation: Spot on! The joints 'react' to the earlier gut infection with inflammation. You are really mastering these tricky complications! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T010#GNS227_U3_T010_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT measured by GDP or GNP?

options.A: Total market value of goods
options.B: Total income generated by businesses
options.C: Overall population health and happiness
options.D: Monetary value of services rendered

explanation: GDP and GNP only measure money and production. They don't capture human well-being, happiness, or social health directly. [learn more](GST322_U3_T1#GST322_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is home delivery not recommended as a default option for every pregnant woman?

options.A: Government policies ban home births completely
options.B: Hospitals prefer to keep all pregnant women admitted
options.C: Unforeseen complications can arise suddenly during labor
options.D: Traditional birth attendants charge too much money

explanation: Labor can become unpredictable very quickly, making facility care necessary for women who develop unexpected risks. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which type of cell division is responsible for producing sperm and egg cells?

options.A: Meiosis
options.B: Osmosis
options.C: Binary fission
options.D: Mitosis

explanation: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half, creating specialized reproductive cells needed for sexual reproduction. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the main goal of taking a nutritional supplement?

options.A: To add extra dietary ingredients to a person's daily intake
options.B: To cure chronic infectious diseases overnight
options.C: To completely replace the need for eating solid foods
options.D: To act as a prescribed pharmaceutical medication

explanation: Supplements are meant to add to your normal meals, not replace them! They give your body a little extra boost of vitamins or minerals when needed. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h1)

question: What is the main goal of Intermittent Preventive Treatment in pregnancy (IPTp)?

options.A: To prevent the woman from ever being bitten by a mosquito
options.B: To boost the production of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: To cure a severe case of cerebral malaria in the third trimester
options.D: To clear hidden parasites and protect the mother and baby

explanation: Spot on! IPTp is given during antenatal care to keep pregnant mums and their babies safe from the hidden dangers of malaria. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the normal, healthy pH range for human blood?
explanation: Memorize this tiny golden window! Staying between 7.35 and 7.45 keeps all our body enzymes working happily. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T11#GNS121_U2_T11_h5)

question: Getting patients out of bed early (early ambulation) mainly helps prevent which dangerous complication?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Excessive hair growth
options.C: Chronic high blood sugar
options.D: Kidney stone formation

explanation: Walking contracts the leg muscles, pumping blood back to the heart and stopping dangerous blood clots from forming in the veins. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h6)

question: What best defines an accident in community health terms?

options.A: A planned medical procedure with complications
options.B: A chronic disease with a slow onset
options.C: An unexpected event causing injury or harm
options.D: An unavoidable natural health disaster

explanation: Accidents are sudden, unexpected events that cause physical harm or damage to individuals. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h1)

question: What is the correct emergency action if a patient takes a sublingual nitroglycerin tablet and their chest pain doesn't go away?

options.A: Wait five minutes, take a second tablet, and call for emergency help if needed
options.B: Take a deep breath and continue the physical exercise they were doing
options.C: Wait twenty minutes for the medicine to absorb before doing anything else
options.D: Swallow three tablets at once immediately and lie flat on the floor

explanation: The golden rule for nitro is: take one tablet every 5 minutes (up to 3 total). If pain persists after the very first one, call emergency services right away! [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which of these is a common sign of psychological trauma in a displaced child?

options.A: An intense desire to learn foreign languages
options.B: Sudden withdrawal, bedwetting, or clingy behavior
options.C: An unexpected increase in academic test scores
options.D: A sudden preference for eating spicy local foods

explanation: Trauma often shows up as regressive behaviors in kids, such as bedwetting, acting extra clingy, or withdrawing from others. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T20#GNS225_U5_T20_h5)

question: When is an autocratic leadership style most appropriate in a clinical setting?

options.A: When planning monthly work rosters
options.B: During routine staff meetings
options.C: When mentoring a new nursing student
options.D: During a sudden cardiac arrest

explanation: High-pressure emergencies require quick, centralized command and clear orders, making autocratic leadership necessary. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why do new mothers need close nursing watch right after delivery?

options.A: Because the mother is at high risk for hemorrhage and infection
options.B: Because the newborn baby requires constant intravenous fluids
options.C: Because mothers cannot produce milk during the first week
options.D: Because routine vital signs are no longer necessary after birth

explanation: The body goes through massive changes right after birth, making those early hours prime time for bleeding and infections. Vigilance saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h6)

question: How many core elements make up the standard post-abortion care framework?

options.A: Ten
options.B: Three
options.C: Seven
options.D: Five

explanation: You got it! The standard PAC framework is built on five key elements that guide clinical care and community support. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h2)

question: What is the main goal of doing a situation analysis in community health nursing?

options.A: To gather comprehensive data about population health and resources
options.B: To punish local leaders for failing to meet health targets
options.C: To replace traditional healers with western medical doctors
options.D: To enforce strict government regulations on local businesses

explanation: Spot on! Before planning any care, you need to understand the community's actual health status and available resources so your efforts hit the mark. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary driving force for providers in a free market healthcare system?

options.A: State control
options.B: Fixed budgeting
options.C: Equal access
options.D: Financial profit

explanation: In a market-based system, the profit motive encourages private entities to invest, innovate, and compete for patients. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h1)

question: What causes the sudden symptoms of Katayama fever (acute schistosomiasis)?

options.A: The immediate accumulation of snail toxins inside the human bloodstream
options.B: A secondary bacterial infection entering through skin puncture sites
options.C: The migration and development of immature worms through tissues
options.D: The sudden death of adult worms inside the intestinal lumen

explanation: Katayama fever is basically your immune system throwing a fit as young worms travel through your body tissues and blood. Your body is fighting hard! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h4)

question: What does a 'just culture' mean for patient safety in a hospital?

options.A: A strict legal system where every single mistake results in immediate court prosecution
options.B: An administrative rule that hides medical errors from patients and their families
options.C: A policy that protects senior doctors from ever facing disciplinary action
options.D: A work environment where staff can report errors openly to fix system flaws without unfair punishment

explanation: In a just culture, nurses feel safe speaking up about mistakes without fear, helping the whole team learn and protect patients better. [learn more](GST321_U1_T2#GST321_U1_T2_h8)

question: Why does a nurse test tear pH with paper before treating a chemical splash?

options.A: To determine if the patient needs local numbing eye drops first
options.B: To prove that the patient is experiencing a severe allergic reaction
options.C: To measure how severe the chemical exposure is and guide treatment
options.D: To check if the patient has a hidden bacterial eye infection

explanation: Checking the pH tells you if it was an acid or an alkali burn, and you keep washing until the pH goes back to normal. Smart nursing! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of getting a CT scan or MRI for a neurological patient?

options.A: Measuring electrical wave patterns during sleep cycles
options.B: Providing detailed structural images of the brain tissue
options.C: Checking cranial nerve function in unconscious patients
options.D: Testing superficial and deep tendon reflex strength

explanation: CT and MRI scans let doctors see cross-section pictures of what is happening inside the skull, like bleeding, swelling, or tumors. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h8)

question: Why do many terminal patients and their families choose home-based palliative care?

options.A: It guarantees that the terminal illness will suddenly go into full remission
options.B: It allows the patient to spend time in a familiar environment with loved ones
options.C: It is completely free with zero financial planning required
options.D: It removes the need for any nursing involvement whatsoever

explanation: Being at home offers comfort and surrounds the patient with familiar people and belongings during end-of-life stages. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why is planning ahead for disasters so crucial instead of just reacting when patients arrive?

options.A: Reacting on the spot is illegal under standard Nigerian healthcare labor laws
options.B: Casualties never arrive at a hospital unless an advanced warning schedule is posted
options.C: Pre-planning prevents the chaos and confusion that lead to preventable deaths during emergencies
options.D: Waiting for patients to arrive guarantees that medical supplies will never run out

explanation: Think of it like studying for exams early! Planning sets clear roles and routines, stopping a hectic situation from turning into a life-threatening disaster. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of infection control rules in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: To ensure that patients clean their own rooms after surgery
options.B: To establish clear standards that protect staff and patients from harm
options.C: To limit the purchase of expensive imported medical equipment
options.D: To reduce the number of nursing shifts required in each ward

explanation: Hospital policies are there to guide safe habits and keep everyone—both nurses and patients—free from avoidable infections. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h8)

question: What is the main benefit of connecting new parents with community support groups?

options.A: Ensuring the nurse no longer needs to visit the home
options.B: Providing free financial assistance for all household expenses
options.C: Reducing feelings of isolation and sharing practical experiences
options.D: Replacing the need for routine pediatric medical checkups

explanation: You got it! Support groups let parents share everyday struggles, find emotional encouragement, and learn great tips from other parents. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h6)

question: Why are latent conditions considered especially dangerous in a healthcare setting?

options.A: They guarantee that a fatal patient outcome will happen daily
options.B: They only affect experienced nurses and senior doctors
options.C: They remain hidden in the system until an accident occurs
options.D: They are easy to fix but hospital managers ignore them

explanation: Well done! Latent conditions sit quietly in the background like hidden traps until the right mix of circumstances triggers an error. [learn more](GST319_U5_T6#GST319_U5_T6_h3)

question: A young teenager is diagnosed with a rare ovarian tumor that starts from the cells that make eggs. What type of tumor is this?

options.A: Germ cell tumor
options.B: Stromal tumor
options.C: Squamous cell tumor
options.D: Epithelial tumor

explanation: Great thinking! Germ cell tumors arise from the egg-producing cells and are more commonly seen in younger patients. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h2)

question: A patient taking amlodipine notices mild swelling in their ankles. What should you tell them?

options.A: Prepare the patient for emergency hospitalization due to acute congestive heart failure
options.B: Tell the patient to stop taking the medication immediately because their kidneys are failing
options.C: Explain that this is a common, non-dangerous side effect caused by blood vessel relaxation
options.D: Advise the patient to restrict their daily fluid intake to less than 500 milliliters

explanation: Brilliant! Ankle swelling (peripheral edema) is a harmless side effect of amlodipine caused by blood vessels opening up wide, not because the heart is failing. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T2#GNS223_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is high out-of-pocket spending dangerous for ordinary citizens?

options.A: It makes doctors prescribe too many generic medications
options.B: It lowers the total number of registered nurses
options.C: It forces families into financial ruin during sudden illness
options.D: It prevents the government from collecting any taxes

explanation: When patients must pay directly out of pocket for every service, medical bills can easily drain family savings and cause poverty. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h1)

question: What actually happens during an in-vitro fertilization (IVF) procedure?

options.A: Sperm are placed directly into the uterus using a small catheter
options.B: Blocked fallopian tubes are surgically tied and opened
options.C: Eggs and sperm are fertilized together in a laboratory dish
options.D: Hormone injections are given to stop natural ovulation

explanation: With IVF, eggs are collected, mixed with sperm in a lab dish to fertilize, and the resulting embryo is placed into the uterus. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T23#GNS312_U1_T23_h6)

question: How do weight-bearing exercises protect an older adult's skeletal system?

options.A: They increase the production of synovial fluid to maximum levels
options.B: They stimulate bone remodeling and strengthen supporting muscles
options.C: They dissolve excess calcium deposits in the joint capsules
options.D: They completely stop the natural aging of joint cartilage

explanation: When bones feel a little bit of working stress, it signals them to stay strong and dense. Exercise is medicine! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T24#GNS222_U1_T24_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of community herd immunity?

options.A: To guarantee lifelong immunity against common viral colds
options.B: To protect vulnerable individuals who cannot safely receive vaccines
options.C: To ensure pharmaceutical companies produce enough medication
options.D: To completely eliminate the need for hand hygiene in hospitals

explanation: When most of the community is vaccinated, germs struggle to spread, shielding babies or sick patients who cannot get immunized. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h6)

question: What do we call the body's natural ability to keep its internal environment balanced and stable?

options.A: Homeostasis
options.B: Catabolism
options.C: Anabolism
options.D: Metabolism

explanation: Homeostasis is like the body's internal thermostat—it constantly works behind the scenes to keep everything stable, no matter what is happening around you! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h1)

question: What usually pushes a struggling endocrine system into a severe crisis like myxedema coma?

options.A: An added physical stressor like an infection or surgery
options.B: Taking a normal scheduled dose of hormone pills
options.C: Eating too much sodium in a single daily meal
options.D: Engaging in light walking exercises in the morning

explanation: When the body is already low on hormones, an extra stressor—like getting sick or having surgery—can completely overwhelm it and trigger a crisis. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h7)

question: Which category of healthcare waste includes discarded scalpels and broken glass ampoules?

options.A: Sharps
options.B: Pharmaceutical waste
options.C: Pathological waste
options.D: General waste

explanation: Sharps are any objects that can puncture or cut skin, including needles, surgical blades, and broken glass vials. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h2)

question: What makes an event count as a natural disaster in healthcare?

options.A: Any medical emergency involving more than ten patients at once
options.B: A minor incident managed easily by standard daily staffing
options.C: An event that overwhelms local healthcare and community resources
options.D: An accident that occurs only within a hospital or clinic setting

explanation: A natural disaster is marked by its ability to stretch local resources past their breaking point, meaning outside help is needed to handle the health crisis. You've got this! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T6#GNS315_U1_T6_h1)

question: How does GNP treat profits earned by a foreign-owned company operating inside Nigeria?

options.A: They are added directly to Nigeria's GNP
options.B: They are converted into government bonds
options.C: They are doubled in Nigeria's GNP
options.D: They are excluded from Nigeria's GNP

explanation: Remember, GNP only counts output generated by citizens and permanent residents, so foreign-owned production inside the country is left out. [learn more](GST322_U3_T1#GST322_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the main goal of a descriptive research design?

options.A: To accurately document characteristics of a population or situation
options.B: To test the effectiveness of a new surgical procedure
options.C: To prove that variable A causes a change in variable B
options.D: To compare two different patient groups after an intervention

explanation: Great job! Descriptive studies are all about painting a clear picture of what is going on right now, without needing to dig into the 'why' or 'how'. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T8#GNS224_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which of these is a common myth about infection control in home settings?

options.A: That handwashing helps reduce bacterial spread
options.B: That family members can transmit respiratory viruses
options.C: That the home environment is naturally germ-free
options.D: That used needles require special puncture-proof containers

explanation: Don't be fooled—homes are not naturally sterile! Good cleaning and hygiene habits are still a must everywhere. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T9#GNS324_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which tiny projections form the brush border right on the surface of intestinal cells?

options.A: Villi
options.B: Microvilli
options.C: Plicae circulares
options.D: Lacteals

explanation: You got it! Microvilli are microscopic hair-like folds right on the enterocytes that create a 'brush border' to maximize how much your gut can absorb. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T012#GNS227_U1_T012_h2)

question: You notice several patients in the surgical ward getting wound infections with similar signs. What should you do right away?

options.A: Report the cluster following hospital infection control protocols and review aseptic techniques.
options.B: Discharge all current patients immediately to close down the hospital wing.
options.C: Prescribe stronger antibiotics to all hospital staff members.
options.D: Wait until the end of the month to see if the infection rate drops naturally.

explanation: Catching an outbreak early is key! Always report the cluster to infection control and check your aseptic techniques to protect your patients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T87#GNS214_U1_T87_h7)

question: At what point during your shift should you separate hospital waste?

options.A: Only when the local sanitation truck arrives
options.B: During final transport outside the hospital gates
options.C: After all waste is mixed together in the utility room
options.D: At the exact moment and place of generation

explanation: Always sort waste right at the bedside as you create it! Waiting until later increases the risk of mistakes and accidental injuries. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h5)

question: What is the main protective antibody packed inside colostrum?

options.A: Immunoglobulin E
options.B: Immunoglobulin A
options.C: Immunoglobulin D
options.D: Immunoglobulin G

explanation: Brilliant! Secretory IgA lines the baby's tummy and intestines, giving them a strong shield against germs. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T18#GNS121_U5_T18_h5)

question: What three areas does the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) assess?

options.A: Blood pressure, heart rate, and temperature
options.B: Swallowing reflex, pupil size, and skin color
options.C: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response
options.D: Pain tolerance, mood, and cognitive memory

explanation: The GCS is a quick, reliable way to check a patient's level of consciousness by testing these three clear reactions. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h7)

question: Why is Type O-negative blood considered the universal red cell donor?

options.A: The blood type is the most common found in humans
options.B: The red blood cells lack A, B, and Rh antigens
options.C: The red blood cells have no hemoglobin inside them
options.D: The plasma contains high levels of protective platelets

explanation: Because Type O-negative red blood cells carry none of the major antigens, recipient antibodies have nothing to react against. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why doesn't full milk production start until after the baby and placenta are delivered?

options.A: The infant's cry is required to wake up the dormant pituitary gland
options.B: The mammary ducts do not form until the exact moment of birth
options.C: Prolactin is entirely absent from the maternal bloodstream until labor
options.D: High pregnancy hormones during gestation block full milk secretion

explanation: Spot on! While pregnant, high levels of estrogen and progesterone act like a block on full milk production. Once the placenta is out, that block is removed! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T14#GNS121_U5_T14_h8)

question: Why do many pregnant women complain of lower back pain and wobbly joints?

options.A: Excess weight causes rapid cartilage breakdown in the knees
options.B: Relaxin softens ligaments all over the body, not just the pelvis
options.C: The growing fetus puts direct pressure on the spinal vertebrae
options.D: Calcium is actively pulled out of the joints to build fetal bones

explanation: You nailed it. Because relaxin circulates everywhere, joints all over the body become looser, meaning supporting muscles have to work extra hard (hello, backache!). [learn more](GNS121_U5_T14#GNS121_U5_T14_h6)

question: What is a major safety challenge unique to home health nursing compared to working in a hospital ward?

options.A: Working alone in unsupervised, unfamiliar community environments
options.B: Lacking access to electronic health charting systems entirely
options.C: Being barred from performing physical assessments on patients
options.D: Having no responsibility for coordinating multidisciplinary care

explanation: Unlike the structured hospital ward where colleagues are close by, home health nurses often travel and enter private homes completely on their own. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h7)

question: When does a medication error cross the line from a civil mistake into criminal liability?

options.A: When the nurse's actions show reckless disregard for human life.
options.B: When the error results in an extended hospital stay.
options.C: When the patient complains loudly to the ward manager.
options.D: When the hospital management decides to issue a query.

explanation: Ordinary mistakes usually fall under civil negligence, but extreme recklessness that puts lives in grave danger crosses over into criminal territory. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT something you should focus on when writing nursing practice implications?

options.A: Suggesting updates to bedside clinical nursing procedures
options.B: Calculating the personal financial bonuses for the lead researcher
options.C: Recommending changes to nursing school education programs
options.D: Highlighting how patient safety can be improved based on data

explanation: You nailed it! Nursing research is all about better patient care and safer practice—never about pocketing extra cash. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T5#GNS224_U2_T5_h5)

question: A nurse wears gloves while emptying a patient's urinary catheter bag. Which link in the chain of infection is the nurse primarily trying to break?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Infectious agent
options.C: Mode of transmission
options.D: Susceptible host

explanation: Wearing gloves creates a barrier that stops germs from moving from the urine to the nurse's hands and onto other surfaces or patients. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical symptom of bacterial food poisoning?

options.A: Sudden bone fracture
options.B: Watery or bloody diarrhea
options.C: Severe abdominal cramps
options.D: Nausea and vomiting

explanation: Foodborne illness hits your gut, causing tummy cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea—it doesn't cause broken bones! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T011#GNS227_U3_T011_h7)

question: Which of the following describes a primary data collection method?

options.A: Reading a published textbook summary of historical mortality rates
options.B: Interviewing patients directly after surgery for a new study
options.C: Downloading a public census file from a government website
options.D: Extracting anonymized blood pressure logs from old hospital archives

explanation: Primary data is gathered firsthand by the researcher specifically to answer their own current research question. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h4)

question: What do we call the path germs use to leave their reservoir?

options.A: Mode of transmission
options.B: Susceptible host
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Portal of exit

explanation: Just like leaving a room through a door, germs use a 'portal of exit' (like coughing or through body fluids) to leave their host. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the relaxation of pelvic joints and ligaments during pregnancy?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Relaxin
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Relaxin works on connective tissue and ligaments to loosen the pelvic girdle in preparation for childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h5)

question: About what fraction of hospital waste is actually hazardous?

options.A: 10 to 25 percent
options.B: Almost 100 percent
options.C: 50 to 60 percent
options.D: 75 to 90 percent

explanation: Most hospital waste is regular trash! Only a small fraction (about 10 to 25 percent) is dangerous and needs special handling. [learn more](GST114_U6_T8#GST114_U6_T8_h1)

question: How is Type 2 diabetes different from Type 1?

options.A: Type 1 can be cured entirely with proper diet and oral medication
options.B: Type 2 only affects elderly individuals who consume high amounts of sugar
options.C: Type 2 involves insulin resistance and relative deficiency rather than complete beta cell destruction
options.D: Type 1 is caused by lifestyle factors while Type 2 is strictly genetic

explanation: In Type 2, the body still makes insulin, but the cells just don't respond to it well (resistance), and the pancreas can't keep up with the extra demand. You're mastering the basics! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h3)

question: What key lifestyle advice should a nurse include when educating a patient with prediabetes?

options.A: Avoid all types of physical movement to preserve energy
options.B: Sleep for at least fourteen hours every single night
options.C: Incorporate a balanced diet and regular physical activity
options.D: Eliminate all forms of water from the daily diet

question: Why do community health nurses view nurseries as valuable health promotion sites?

question: Which health issues are most common among children in chronically vulnerable homes?

question: Why is it always smart to let a friend read your draft before you submit it?

question: What common allergy must you always check for before using a standard urinary catheter?

question: Who is most important to involve when trying to change harmful food taboos in a rural community?

question: Why do the veins in your limbs have one-way valves inside them?

question: What are the classic warning signs of phlebitis at an IV site?

question: Why do nurses need to understand the basic chemistry of food nutrients?

question: Why must you follow the manufacturer's recommended contact time for a disinfectant?

question: What is an adverse event?

question: Which practice helps a disaster nurse stay strong and prevent burnout while responding to a crisis?

question: What is the main purpose of 'informed choice' in nursing practice?

question: Why shouldn't a patient suddenly stop taking sleeping pills after using them for months?

question: A doctor prescribes a topical medication for a patient's oily, acne-prone face. Which form will you most likely give them?

options.C: Ointment
options.D: Gel

question: What type of drug binds to a receptor and blocks other substances from activating it?

question: Why is activated charcoal often instilled right before the lavage tube is removed?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common risk of healthcare outsourcing?

options.C: Difficulty in monitoring complex vendor performance contracts

question: What is a major clinical indication for the immediate emergency referral of a pregnant woman?

options.B: Mild morning sickness during the first trimester
options.C: Physiological ankle swelling after long standing
options.D: Normal vertex presentation at 36 weeks

explanation: Severe pre-eclampsia poses an immediate, life-threatening risk of seizures and stroke, requiring urgent transfer to a facility capable of managing complications. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why might a misguided healthcare worker agree to perform FGM?

question: What is the standard first-line injection used to treat uncomplicated gonorrhea?

options.A: Ceftriaxone
options.B: Penicillin G

options.D: Vancomycin

question: Why do healthy pregnant women need to produce more insulin as their pregnancy advances?

options.C: Placental hormones make maternal cells more resistant to insulin
options.D: Maternal kidneys begin to excrete insulin much faster

question: What is one of the main roles of a community health nurse in an intersectoral team?

options.A: Acting as a bridge connecting community members with other developmental sectors
options.B: Managing hospital budgets for the entire state health ministry
options.C: Taking over the administrative duties of local government chairpersons
options.D: Constructing boreholes and building roads without outside assistance

explanation: Right! Nurses serve as the vital link between health needs and sectors like water, education, and agriculture to solve problems together. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h4)

question: Which nursing goal for a malnourished patient is written clearly and measurably?

options.A: Patient will stop refusing meals when nurses enter

options.C: Patient will gain ten pounds of pure muscle by tomorrow morning

question: A patient asks you for antibiotics to treat a mild cold (a virus). How should you reply?

options.A: Advise the patient to take a double dose to clear the viral symptoms faster
options.B: Encourage the patient to find a different clinic that will prescribe the medication

question: Where should community-based mental health interventions ideally take place to be most effective?

options.A: Exclusively inside high-security psychiatric hospital wards

options.C: Only through remote internet video calls managed by government agencies

question: How is child trafficking different from regular help on a family farm?

options.A: Trafficking always involves coercion and exploitation
options.B: Trafficking only happens in urban city centers
options.C: Normal labor is strictly illegal for all minors
options.D: Normal labor pays a much higher daily wage

explanation: While helping out with family chores or learning a trade can be safe, trafficking relies on deceit, force, and taking advantage of a child against their will. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T25#GNS225_U5_T25_h1)

question: A patient has widespread body pain, tender points, and ongoing fatigue, but no visible joint swelling. What condition fits best?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Osteoarthritis
options.C: Fibromyalgia
options.D: Gout

explanation: Fibromyalgia is known for widespread pain and tender points, but unlike arthritis, it doesn't cause joint swelling or deformity. Great to keep this distinction in mind! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h3)

question: Which type of research question looks at how two things connect or link together, without saying one causes the other?

options.A: Historical
options.B: Descriptive
options.C: Relational
options.D: Causal

explanation: Relational questions explore the relationship between variables—like asking if nurses' shift lengths relate to fatigue levels—without proving direct cause and effect. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h3)

question: When you are caring for a very sick patient who cannot respond, what is your main job as their nurse?

options.A: Discharging the patient as quickly as possible
options.B: Focusing solely on medication administration schedules
options.C: Waiting for family members to make all clinical decisions
options.D: Acting as the patient's primary defense and surrogate voice

question: What is a major problem with making patients pay cash directly out-of-pocket every time they visit the hospital?

options.A: Hospitals automatically get too much money from foreign donors
options.B: Diseases completely vanish from poor communities
options.C: Patients often delay or avoid getting care because they don't have immediate cash
options.D: The number of nurses in the village instantly doubles

explanation: Spot on. Paying cash right at the counter is a huge barrier for many families, forcing them to stay home and suffer rather than seek help. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic example of an active failure in the clinical area?

options.A: Poorly designed infusion pump software installed hospital-wide
options.B: A nurse giving the wrong dose because of misreading a label
options.C: Chronic staff shortages leading to extreme nurse fatigue
options.D: A hospital purchasing confusingly similar medication vials

explanation: You nailed it! Active failures are immediate actions taken right at the frontline of care. Every question you answer makes you a sharper nurse! [learn more](GST319_U5_T6#GST319_U5_T6_h3)

question: What are the standard settings for a hospital autoclave?

options.A: 72 degrees Celsius for 15 seconds

options.C: 160 degrees Celsius with dry heat
options.D: 121 degrees Celsius at 15 psi

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations is an example of which level of prevention?

question: Which part of the peripheral nervous system controls voluntary skeletal muscle movement?

question: Which group of people has the highest risk of catching hydatid disease?

question: Which of these nursing actions is a good example of primary disease prevention?

options.B: Screening adults for high blood pressure
options.C: Treating complications of chronic stroke
options.D: Isolating a patient with active tuberculosis

explanation: You got it! Primary prevention stops a disease before it even starts—and immunizations are the classic example. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T13#GNS313_U1_T13_h6)

question: What is a major benefit of using Electronic Health Records (EHR) instead of paper?

options.B: Simultaneous access by multiple healthcare providers

options.D: Immunity from computer viruses and power outages

question: Which class of medication is usually given first for obsessive-compulsive neurosis?

options.C: Short-acting barbiturate sedatives
options.D: Atypical antipsychotic medications

explanation: You got it! SSRIs are the go-to drugs to help balance serotonin levels and dial down those intense symptoms. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T7#GNS314_U2_T7_h5)

question: When is the best time to label a collected laboratory specimen?

question: What do the letters in the SBAR communication tool stand for?

question: What is another common name for non-specific body defences?

question: Which of the following structures works closely with the vestibular cortex to maintain posture?

question: Which of these is a common acquired (later in life) cause of a shortened fallopian tube?

question: When the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) kicks in, what is its main job?

question: Which hormone imbalance is a main trigger for most endometrial cancers?

question: A patient taking warfarin has a dangerously high INR and mild bleeding. What will the medical team most likely give?

question: In healthcare technology, what is the main goal of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI)?

question: When does an Rh-negative person usually develop anti-Rh antibodies?

question: What is the single most effective way to stop the spread of infections in the hospital?

question: An imperforate hymen causing primary amenorrhoea is a physical blockage in which part of the body?

question: How does tuberculosis mostly spread from one person to another?

question: How is active surveillance different from passive surveillance?

question: What approach should a nurse use when caring for a patient experiencing complications from a harmful traditional practice?

question: What is the primary clinical use of a weighing scale in routine nursing care?

question: How often should temperature checks typically be performed on individuals in quarantine?

question: Why does milk production stop when a baby is abruptly weaned?

question: What is the big advantage when a baby's head is fully flexed?

question: You are getting ready to change a surgical wound dressing on a patient's kitchen table. What action shows proper technique?

question: Why do healthcare workers set a clear 'case definition' during a disease outbreak?

question: What is the main reason healthcare providers use drug classification systems?

question: Why do our hands and face get a much larger area on the sensory homunculus than our back or thighs?

question: What is the first-line medication of choice for treating a severe anaphylactic drug reaction?

question: Why is drug distribution so important for a medication to work?

question: How is the bed arranged when a patient is placed in the Trendelenburg position?

question: What is the main goal when using a qualitative research design?

question: What is the very first sign a nurse looks for on a growth chart to spot growth faltering?

question: What does the letter 'D' stand for in the ABCDE primary survey?

question: What weather condition in tropical regions like Nigeria contributes greatly to skin fungal infections?

question: A patient comes in with fever, right upper tummy pain, dark urine, and yellow eyes a few weeks after getting injections at an unlicensed clinic. What is the most likely condition?
